question: The concept of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India is inspired by which country's constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Soviet Union**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties were incorporated into the Indian Constitution via the **42nd Amendment Act** in 1976.
 
• This concept was inspired by the Constitution of the former **Soviet Union**, which emphasized the duties of citizens alongside their rights.
 
• Initially, 10 Fundamental Duties were included; an additional duty was added later through the **86th Amendment Act** in 2002.
 
• Fundamental Duties are listed under **Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution and serve as moral obligations for citizens.
 
• The aim is to promote a sense of responsibility and national unity among Indian citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42nd Amendment Act (1976):**

 
 
• Known as the "Mini Constitution," it introduced several significant changes, including Fundamental Duties, the Preamble, and changes to the Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
• The Fundamental Duties were added based on the recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee**.
 
 
 
• **Article 51A:**
 
 
• It lists 11 Fundamental Duties, such as respecting the Constitution, promoting harmony, and protecting the environment.
 
 
 
• **86th Amendment Act (2002):**
 
 
• This amendment added the duty of providing opportunities for education to children between the ages of 6 to 14 years.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• While many constitutions focus predominantly on rights, the Soviet Union emphasized both rights and duties to ensure collective responsibility.
 
• India adopted a similar approach to align with its socio-cultural ethos and promote civic responsibility.
